ApprovalApprove.description:
The written reason of an approve and, for a sole decide-holder, the acknowledgement and
the digest of the action they were shown.
ApprovalApprove.title: ApprovalApprove

ApprovalDecision.description:
A human's answer to an approval request. The solo fields are read only when `approve` is
true.
ApprovalDecision.title: ApprovalDecision

ApprovalMode.description:
Who could have decided. It grants nothing and is never
read to allow an action. `escalated` and `break_glass` are reserved words that nothing
writes yet.
ApprovalMode.title: ApprovalMode

ApprovalReason.description: The written reason of a reject; the verb is in the path.
ApprovalReason.title: ApprovalReason

AssignmentBody.description: A model for an agent or role; `model` null clears the ledger assignment.
AssignmentBody.title: AssignmentBody

AssignmentPutBody.description: The body of `PUT /v1/models/assignments/{scope}/{id}`: scope and id are in the path.
AssignmentPutBody.title: AssignmentPutBody

ChallengeBody.description: The challenge a password login answered.
ChallengeBody.title: ChallengeBody

ConfirmBody.description: The pending factor and a code from the authenticator app.
ConfirmBody.title: ConfirmBody

ConnectionBody.description:
A connection. Nothing else is accepted, so no secret and no file path can be sent; `key`
is the *name* of an operator key binding.
ConnectionBody.title: ConnectionBody

DisableBody.description: Why a person switches a breaker off: one of four fixed codes, never free text.
DisableBody.title: DisableBody

EditBody.description: A change of an entry's family and/or processing scope.
EditBody.title: EditBody

GrantBody.description: A grant request: what the person read (`as_of`, `ledger_position`, `evidence_hash`).
GrantBody.title: GrantBody

IssueBody.description: A new credential: its scopes (`read`, `run`; duplicates are merged) and lifetime in days.
IssueBody.title: IssueBody

LoginBody.description: Email and password. Limits keep the body small; wrong shapes are still a plain 401.
LoginBody.title: LoginBody

LoginConfirmBody.description: The challenge, the pending factor and a code from the authenticator app.
LoginConfirmBody.title: LoginConfirmBody

LoginMfaBody.description: A challenge and exactly one of a TOTP code and an MFA recovery code.
LoginMfaBody.title: LoginMfaBody

NewTokenBody.description:
A new API token. `name` is a label for the program or purpose (`ci-nightly`), **not a
person's name** and should not be personal data; the ledger never holds it (it records
`service:<id>`).
Reserved: `cli`, `system`, `api`, `engine` and anything starting `tok_`.
NewTokenBody.title: NewTokenBody

OptionalReasonBody.description: A body whose only field is an optional reason.
OptionalReasonBody.title: OptionalReasonBody

PasswordCodeBody.description: The password entered again and a TOTP code.
PasswordCodeBody.title: PasswordCodeBody

PasswordConfirmBody.description:
`{password}` and nothing else. 1 to 1024 characters after NFKC (main's own limit), with a
cheap bound of 4096 UTF-8 bytes first. Errors never carry the input back.
PasswordConfirmBody.title: PasswordConfirmBody

PlanItem.description: One task of an API plan. Ids are assigned by the server (`<run_id>-t<n>`).
PlanItem.title: PlanItem

PriceBody.description:
One price version. Rates are decimal text; a JSON number is refused. The bound endpoint
is set by the service and a body that names it is refused.
PriceBody.title: PriceBody

code.description: the stable machine name of the error

PromptCacheBody.description: Turn provider-side prompt caching on or off for the organization.
PromptCacheBody.title: PromptCacheBody

QuoteBody.description: A plan: one entry per planned task, with the role of its assignee, provider and model.
QuoteBody.title: QuoteBody

RefBody.description: An entry named by provider and model (approve, pause, retire, remove).
RefBody.title: RefBody

RoleBody.description:
The new role. Any string is accepted here; the service answers 422 for anything but
`viewer` and `approver` (and `role_not_assignable` for `owner`, which comes first).
RoleBody.title: RoleBody

RotateBody.description: Rotate: the new lifetime in days and the overlap in seconds. Scopes cannot change.
RotateBody.title: RotateBody

SetKeyBody.description: `value` is write-only: it is never in a response, an error or the ledger.
SetKeyBody.title: SetKeyBody

SetupBody.description: The one-time setup token with the first owner's chosen details.
SetupBody.title: SetupBody

StopRequestBody.description: A human asks a run to stop. The reason is optional; the ledger keeps only its hash.
StopRequestBody.title: StopRequestBody

Unblock.description: A human lifts a budget block, optionally with a higher limit.
Unblock.title: Unblock

code.description: the stable machine name of the error

nuramesh__server__app__EmptyBody.description: No body, or `{}`: the org safety actions that take nothing.
nuramesh__server__app__EmptyBody.title: EmptyBody

nuramesh__server__auth__EmptyBody.description: Mutations carry an empty JSON object (the guard requires a JSON body).
nuramesh__server__auth__EmptyBody.title: EmptyBody

cheaper model where the evidence supports it. Read-only and scoped to the

Runs, most recently active first (`limit` at most 200): `{"runs": [...], "truncated",
"scanned"}`. Each row has the status, task and gate counts and the spend, derived from the
run's ledger (the REST API guide). `status` is one of the documented values (else 422).
The work per request is bounded; `truncated` says the bound stopped the search.

post.description:
A person starts a run. Asynchronous: the plan's text goes to
the content store (never the ledger), a start request is stored and the answer is 202; a
runner checks the plan against the team's code and begins it, or refuses it visibly in
`GET /v1/runs/{id}`. The run id is the server's: with an `Idempotency-Key` it is derived
from (organization, actor, route, key), so a retry is the same run.

One run: status, tasks with their gates and verdicts, attempts, spend, budgets. A run
that is only a start request (a runner has not begun it yet, or refused it) shows the
request: `state` `requested` or `refused` with a `refusal_code`.

The run's ledger stream, paged; `type` keeps entries whose type starts with it
(for example `gate.` or `budget.`).

post.description:
A person, a `run` token or an agent credential asks the run to stop
(`run.stop_requested`, the actor from the credential only). Idempotent: asking again
returns the first request and writes nothing. The engine ends the run cleanly at its next
step. An agent may stop only a run it takes part in (it is the assignee of a task of the
run); any other run of the organization is answered exactly as a run that does not exist,
before the finished check, and the same is checked again inside the write
transaction.

post.description:
A person decides a human gate that a durable run waits on. The answer never contains the
person's text. The record is written on a worker thread; waking the workflow (a network
call, a few seconds at most) happens on its own small pool, so a slow Temporal cannot hold
up the threads that authorize every other request.

The organization's only person who can decide sends `acknowledge_solo: true` with a
decision that passes the gate (403 `acknowledge_required` otherwise; a failing decision
needs nothing more).

Renamed to `/v1/runs/{run_id}/tasks/{task_id}/gates/{gate_id}/decisions`.
